pageCache.text:
New Starters - September Intake
Welcome to Lambs Lane School!
For those families who are offered a place at Lambs Lane School for Reception in September we will try to give you as much information as we can to help your child start school successfully. Please bear in mind that the confirmed list of new starters is not sent over from Wokingham Borough Council until June. Once we have this list further information will be sent to parents.
The Reception Class will be in the Wrens classroom, which has it's an outside play area and garden! It can be accessed from the main playground via a gate. This is where parents and carers drop off in the morning and pick up from after school.
Useful Information.
We are delighted to welcome our new parents and their children as they begin their exciting journey with us here at Lambs Lane. The new parents meeting is designed to give you an introduction to school life, share what to expect in the months ahead, and answer any questions you may have. Our aim is to ensure you feel informed, supported, and confident as your child takes this important step into their school adventure.
Dates for the New Parents meetings (parents only need attend one session):
Tuesday 23rd June 2026 @ 9am in the school hall
Thursday 25th June 2026 @ 5pm in the school hall
New intake transition day - Wednesday 1st July
Your child will be invited to one of the following sessions (details will follow in your welcome pack):
Session 1 from 10am to 12 Noon
Session 2 from 1.30pm to 3.30pm
On Wednesday 1st July (weather permitting) you and your child are invited to our teddy bears picnic. It will give you a chance to meet other parents and some of the Lambs Lane staff. The school catering team - Impact Food - will be preparing some samples for parents and children to sample
Doorstep visits from the class teacher take place at the start of September, on Thursday 3rd and Friday 4th, your allocated time of your visit will be sent to you.
Our EYFS class will start school on Monday 7th September 2026.
Click here to see our current EYFS Team
Starting School
The BBC have some great resources for helping to prepare your child for school.
Click here to find out more.
You can also find lots of useful information on the Wokingham Borough Council website here.
Uniform
You can order your child's uniform online using our suppliers Brigade. For more information about our uniform and how to access the online shop, click here. You can also buy non branded uniform from supermarkets and high street shops.
We have pre-loved uniform for sale at school, if you would like to buy some of our pre-loved uniform please email admin@lambslane.wokingham.sch.uk and we will help you out!
Breakfast and After School Club.
We offer both before and after school wrap around care. If you are interested in using this service, you may want to register your child before September. All the information you need can be found here: Click Here
Travelling to School.
We operate an informal one-way system to try and manage congestion outside school both in the morning and afternoon. Click here to see how it works.
There are many benefits to walking, cycling or scooting to school.
Walking, cycling and Scooting to School
School Milk.
Our school milk scheme. Did you know our school has a school milk scheme?
By registering your child for our school milk scheme they will receive a 189ml (third of a pint) carton of semi-skimmed milk every day. This is delivered fresh and chilled to their classroom every day.
How much does it cost? Thanks to government subsidies, school milk is free for all under-fives and is subsided at around £15 a term for children aged five or older.
Why should I register my child? School milk provides your child with essential nutrients such as calcium and protein, for strong, healthy teeth and bones. It is also rehydrating and energy boosting, helping to bridge the long gap between breakfast and lunch so children stay focused.
How do I register my child? If your child is under five- Go to www.coolmilk.com or pick up a form from school. Just register by a Tuesday for your child’s free milk to start the following week.

Prospective Parent Information
Welcome to Lambs Lane Primary School
At Lambs Lane Primary School, we believe that every child deserves to be encouraged to "Reach out and shine". Our school is a warm and inclusive community where children feel safe, valued, and encouraged to reach their full potential.
We are proud to offer a nurturing environment that combines academic expectations with a strong focus on wellbeing, creativity, and personal development. Our dedicated staff work closely with families to ensure that every child receives the support and challenge they need to thrive.
From engaging classroom experiences to enriching activities in sport, the arts, and outdoor learning, we aim to spark curiosity and build confidence in every pupil. Above all, we want our children to develop a lifelong love of learning and the skills they need to succeed both in school and beyond.
We look forward to welcoming you and your child to the Lambs Lane community.
When we were not able to offer school tours due to covid, we produced the virtual tour below:

Breakfast and After School Club
The Lambs Lane Breakfast and After School Clubs are a Local Authority and Ofsted registered childcare facility for primary aged children, offering a safe, caring and fun environment for children to enjoy outside school hours.
This facility is available during term time only from 7.45am and between 3.30pm and 6.00pm.
Current prices are as follows:
Breakfast Club - Prices
Breakfast Club Bookings from September 2025
Full session £6.50. 7.45am - 8.50am (includes breakfast.)
Half Session £3.00. 8.30am - 8.50am.
Please note breakfast is served until 8.20am.
After School Club - Prices
After School Club Bookings from September 2024
Long Session £13.00 per full session - 3.30pm until 6.00pm.
Intermediate session (after sports club booking) £10.00 4.30pm until 6pm.
One Hour session £6.50 per session - 3.30pm until 4.30pm.
Short Session/Late Collection £3.50 per session - 3.30pm until 4pm.
Please note that if a child is picked up after 4.30pm, the full session fees will be charged. If you pick up your child up after 6pm the school will charge £10 for every 15 minutes thereafter.
Please see the updated Handbook below for full details and the Arbor information as to how you are able to book your wraparound care. For any clarification of queries, please contact Miss Hill or Mrs Pridmore in the school office. bhill@lambslane.wokingham.sch.uk or admin@lambslane.wokingham.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Special Educational Needs (SEN) - Lambs Lane Primary School -
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs (SEN)
Our school community prides itself on having an inclusive nature that is fully embedded. In 2024, we became an Inclusion Quality Mark ‘Flagship School'. The whole school community thrives on and values the diverse nature of the school population. All children at some time in their education might need additional support in a particular area of their learning or within their social and emotional development.
Whatever the need, we will ensure that the appropriate interventions are provided through early identification, a graduated response, and by working closely with parents or carers at all stages of support.
These interventions may take the form of additional support in the classroom, a more structured programme such as ‘Nessy’ for reading and spelling needs, or Nurture support to help develop social and emotional skills. Our Nurture Assistants are trained by Wokingham Educational Psychologists, to deliver sessions to small groups on skills such as self-esteem and working together. Where we require more advice, and in consultation with parents, some children may also receive support from external professionals linked to the Berkshire Health Trust – CYPIT, the Educational Psychology Service, Learning Support Service or Foundry College.
Lambs Lane is also a Resource-based School for pupils with Complex Needs, including those with a physical disability. The school has been adapted to allow easy access to all areas of the school environment and we also house a Physiotherapy and Sensory Room. All pupils are integrated into a mainstream class with their peers, in line with our inclusion ethos, but personalised timetables are implemented according to individual need.
We understand that very able children also may have additional needs and we ensure tasks are planned to challenge these children through greater depth and enrichment activities. We recognise that children may be gifted or talented in one or more areas of the whole curriculum, and opportunities are provided to support their individual needs, either academic, creative or sporting.
If you wish to contact our Inclusion Manager, please see the contact details below:
Email: ccarroll@lambslane.wokingham.sch.uk
Please see below links to our local offer, inclusion and SEN policy, our accessibility plan, our aspiration and achievement document and further information on our resource unit. More detail can also be found in the Disability Code of Practice.
Wokingham Borough Council also have Local Offer for children and young people with additional needs. Click the link below to have a look at their website

Hall & Facilities Hire
School Facilities – Available for hire
Did you know our school facilities are available for hire? Based in Spencers Wood (RG7 1JB) we have been a popular venue for Yoga classes, Bootcamps, Zumba and aerobics classes.
Both the school hall and sports field are available for hire at the following rates:
RATES FOR HIRING SCHOOL PREMISES:
HALL* (with access to toilets in entrance hall)
£25.00 for the first hour
£10.00 for every hour thereafter
The hall is available to hire from 18.00 - 21.00 Monday to Friday. Weekend lettings may be considered on request.
* No access to kitchen. Use of kitchen must be arranged directly with the Contract Caterers via Wokingham Borough Council.
£30.00 per session* (with no access to toilets in school building)
£50.00 per session* (with access to toilets in school building)
* Session: Morning 8.30am - 12.30pm / Afternoon 1.00pm - 5.00pm
£10.00 per session - no access to the building.
We have 2 playgrounds that can be hired, the front smaller playground and also the larger main playground at the rear of the school. Both playgrounds can be accessed without entering the school building.
Sunday lettings: 33% surcharge
Hirer's Liability Insurance: £2.65 or 10.5%, whichever is the greatest*
* Hirers in possession of their own insurance cover that satisfies the specified conditions as stated on the Hire Contract will not be charged.
For further information and availability, please contact the school office:
e-mail: llainsbury@lambslane.wokingham.sch.uk
If you are interested in hiring our hall, playground or field you will need to complete our Letting Form which can be found at the end of our Lettings Policy. Click here to view it in the Policy area of our website.

pageCache.pageTitle: Picture News - Lambs Lane Primary School -
pageCache.text:
Picture News
An area of focus for the school is the development of oracy skills. Whilst competence in the tested areas of the curriculum such as reading, writing and maths is crucial, it is key that children are able to express their thoughts, feeling, knowledge and understanding verbally as well. We are developing a number of strategies to support our children with the development of vocabulary and other oracy strategies such as reasoning and confidence in speaking in front of an audience and one of the resources that we will be using is Picture News.
Each week we will receive some resources related to a current topic. This will include activities for assembly, early morning work and also includes a topic to prompt a conversation at home. We would like to encourage you to share this with your child, perhaps over the evening meal or in a quiet 5 minutes. Staff in school will be following this up the next week and so your support will be invaluable. There is a space for making notes on the worksheet but that is optional.
We hope that you enjoy sharing ideas and opinions with your child and we look forward to hearing them in school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 3 and 4 Residential - Lambs Lane Primary School -
pageCache.text:
Year 3 and 4 Residential
In the Summer Term, usually around June, our Year 3 and 4 class go on a 2 night residential trip. This year, in 2026, our pupils have the exciting opportunity to take part in a residential trip to Ufton Court, a historic Tudor manor set in beautiful woodland.
This hands-on experience brings history and outdoor learning to life, giving children the chance to explore the grounds, take part in team-building challenges, and immerse themselves in themed activities linked to their curriculum.
The trip helps build confidence, independence, and collaboration, all while creating wonderful memories with friends. It is safe, supportive environment where children learn new skills, enjoy the outdoors, and deepen their understanding of the past.
The children are usually accompanied by 2 teachers and at least 3 teaching assistants.
We write a diary while we are away so that parents can see what we have been up to.
We hold an information evening each year and the class also have a presentation about the trip.
Ready for the off in 2018!
Having fun in June 2019.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sports Premium - Lambs Lane Primary School -
pageCache.text:
Sports Premium
PE and Sport Premium Funding
The government has continued to fund PE and Sports Premium to improve physical education (PE) and sport in primary schools. This funding - provided jointly by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport - is allocated to primary school head teachers and must be used to improve the provision of P.E. and school sport.
Please click here for access to the government website.
PE and school sports are an important part of Lambs Lane school life. We believe that PE and school sport contribute to the spiritual, moral, social and communicative development of our children and through participation, our children build and learn more about our key values such as respect, co-operation and kindness for themselves and others. For all children ‘Reach out and Shine’ applies to all aspects of learning at Lambs Lane, with PE being no exception. We acknowledge that a broad, balanced, high quality curriculum has a positive impact on concentration, attitude and achievement. The school strives to offer a sport or activity that each pupil can take part and participate in and enjoy.
Sports Funding for 2025 – 2026
Our overall aim is to raise standards in P.E. and school sport, increasing the participation and opportunities offered to our children. We aim to continue to provide high quality lessons and improved learning for all.
The phase of sport funding 2025 –2026 (£20,448) will be used to develop PE and school sport in the following ways:
2024-2025 Sports Premium Funding
2025-2026 Sports Premium Funding
Increased participation in competitive sport

pageCache.pageTitle: Absence, Attendance and Timekeeping - Lambs Lane Primary School -
pageCache.text:
Absence, Attendance and Timekeeping
The importance of attendance and timekeeping
Good attendance and punctuality are essential for children's learning and wellbeing. When pupil's arrive on time and attend regularly, they settle quickly, feel confident in routines, and make the most of every learning opportunity. Consistent attendance also helps children build strong friendships and keeps their progress on track. By supporting good timekeeping at home, families help children develop positive habits that will benefit them throughout school and beyond.
Reporting an Absence
If your child is unwell or not able to come to school for any reason, the school MUST know on the first day of that absence. Please report any absence by 09.00 where possible using one of the following:
Arbor App - Use the absence button on the parent app or in-app message area.
Email - admin@lambslane.wokingham.sch.uk
Telephone - 0118 9883820 option 1 for the absence reporting answerphone.
Please confirm in detail the reason for absence; do not use poorly, unwell or sick. It is part of our Safeguarding Policy to ensure we know where all our pupils are when not at school.
Any absence that is longer than 2 days must be confirmed in writing (letter, email or In App Message) to ensure your child is recorded as authorised absence.
Attendance Advice and Guidance for Parents/Carers
Please see further guidance on the Wokingham Borough Council Website here.
If your child has a sickness bug we ask that they do not come back to school until they are symptom free for 48 hours.
If your child is sick following, for example a coughing fit, we suggest a 24 hour absence to be sure it isn't a sickness bug.
Medicines in School
f your child has a recurring or infectious illness, please would you let us know. In agreement with the regulations laid down by the Health and Safety at Work Act, the school can only administer 'prescribed medicines' where written consent has been given by a parent. A medicine form can be obtained from the School Office where the medicines should be left each morning. We have been advised that where three doses daily have been prescribed for medicines, there is no reason why the doses cannot be administered before and after school and at bedtime. Where four daily doses are required, we are prepared to administer a dose at lunchtime on behalf of parents.
Should it be necessary for your child to receive medication during school hours, then the medicine should be clearly labelled with your child's name and full details of dosage. The school accepts no liability for such items. Although we have a working practice that staff can administer medicine, staff have the right to refuse to administer the medicine.
Illness
We do not have the facilities for looking after sick children. In the event of illness, we will try to contact parents immediately by phone or text. You should ensure that we have up-to-date information on your Arbor account, how to contact you and an emergency contact number.
Doctor and Hospital Appointments
If your child has a Doctor or Hospital appointment, please notify the school by phone or email as you would for any other absence. Please also provide a copy of the appointment confirmation letter, email or text.
Why is it important for your child to arrive to school on time?
As a result of your child arriving late, they may have missed the following types of learning....
School starts at 09.00. It is important for your child's emotional wellbeing, learning and progress that they arrive in plenty of time for the start of the day. Pupils that arrive after 09.00 will be marked as late "L". Registers currently close at 09.10am, pupils that arrive after this time will be marked as late after registers close "U". U is an unauthorised absence.
Children should be signed in/out of the premises by a responsible adult.
Persistent lateness may be reported to the Educational Welfare Officer.
Please do contact the School Office for guidance and help.
